title: Contemplating whether I should release this Sailing Game
author: keeldragger
selftext: I built this Sailing Game - it's part simulation and part GTA 4, LOL.    However, I'm still on the fence about releasing it as there seems to be a ton of AI-hate out there right now and I'm seeing the market flooded with low effort, AI generated "slop".   I built developed this game as a passion project and heavily used Claude, Codex, and now Antigravity throughout the process.   Everything is built on top of Unity with 3D models processed thru Blender.   What's interesting about this game is that it's hyper-local:  the maps and seas are derived from NOAA maritime charts, the land is derived from airborne and satellite imagery/lidar data, the weather comes from live forecasts.  Local points of interests were modeled using Claude/ChatGpt models to provide additional depth. Sailboats were also modeled in Blender by AI, but they use actual polar and racing handicap data for performance characteristics.  The stars, planets, moon, and sunrise/sunset follow the real constellation placements according to time of day/year.    All of these features took an incredible amount of time to develop a test even with the use of AI tools.  However, I feel like AI games are getting punished.  I've love to get some feedback - does this look like a game that has enough appeal that folks will buy it?  worth continuing to invest and refine to release?  Am I spending too much time on the underlying details that will likely be under appreciated by most players?

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body:
I wouldn't release as-is if you want to beat the slop allegations. It's just not polished enough. Feels like very different levels of detail on different objects. 

Definitely has potential but currently it doesn't seem to be certain of it's identity, if it's a serious sailing sim I wold expect much more fleshed out water physics and graphics.

replies.author: keeldragger
replies.body: That tracks with my thoughts as well.  I've made some improvements since I made that highlight video but your feedback is spot on.
